comparator.name: Psychology (Psychologie)
comparator.sourceNotes: Coherent 2024-entry cohort: B1 in the adopted 2024–25 OER, B2 in the adopted 2025–26 OER, and pre-September-2025 programme B3 in the adopted 2026–27 OER. The 2026–27 reformed B1/B2 cannot be combined with this older B3. Three 60 EC years total 180 EC: 124 compulsory, 40 restricted choice, 16 genuine open electives. B2 selects one period-2 theme (Emotion) and one period-3 theme (Development of Pro- and Antisocial Behaviour), plus the permitted 4 EC B3 elective Consciousness and Perception in B2 period 4. B3 selects Brain & Cognition, its required matching 6 EC domain course and a second 6 EC domain course, 4 EC applied methods, three distinct 4 EC domain electives, 4 EC ethics, 16 EC open space and 12 EC thesis. The B2 elective is not repeated in B3. These are permitted official-order examples, not an individual entitlement or a promised future entrant timetable. Old Dutch tables print the Development & Mental Health practical PSB2DH10EB as 4 EC, conflicting with the year total; the current Dutch transition table explicitly assigns 1 EC, as does the same-year 2025 English table. Use that explicit 1 EC evidence, not arithmetic inference. The prospective third-year page is indicative, totals 60.5 EC and prints career orientation as 0.5 EC; adopted OER has 60 EC and Me & My Career 2 at 0 EC. Hidden metadata and visible annual/cohort headings were checked for all four editions. B1 includes 1 EC for 24 participant hours or an approved replacement, inside its 60 EC. RADAr NL is separately mandatory at 0 EC with no exemption; B2 Me & My Career 1 is 1 EC, B3 Me & My Career 2 is 0 EC. Current B2 entry requires positive or held BSA, B3 positive BSA; normal BSA threshold 42 EC. Statistics 2, Data Analysis and Psychometrics require Statistics 1; the latter two assume Statistics 2 knowledge. RP2 requires Statistics 1, Methods and Research Practicum 1, with Statistics 2 assumed. Ethics requires 90 EC psychology. Applied methods requires Statistics 1 and assumes Statistics 2/Psychometrics. Thesis requires 119 EC including Statistics 2, RP2 and full B1 60 EC including participant hours; Data Analysis, Psychometrics and Applied Methods assumed. Thesis normally follows selected domain; another domain needs Board permission. Exchange starts in B3 with full B1 including participation obtained six months before departure. Timely registration and course capacities apply.

core: Psychological foundations of thinking, emotion, motivation, behaviour and social relationships
Brain, cognition, perception and memory with the first-listed Brain & Cognition domain
Empirical and experimental research, statistics, psychometrics and the bachelor thesis
Human development, mental health, psychodiagnostics and behaviour change
adjacent: Clinical assessment, psychological treatment and mental-health across the lifespan
Psychology of organisations, work, social influence and leadership
Educational and school contexts of psychological development
questions: How do social and motivational processes shape behaviour, including habits and health decisions?
How do psychologists assess and support mental health across development?
How do cognition and social settings shape learning and work?

courses: New Issues in Contemporary Social Theory
trace: Foundational psychology and neural function, nature/nurture and methods; substantial introductory contribution.
Classical sociology, race/gender/class and historical context; social complement, not social psychology.
Cells, molecular biology and physiology provide biological background; no psychology equivalence.
Scientific social psychology: attitudes, groups and interpersonal behaviour; direct psychological content, description-only evidence limits specificity.
Research design, sampling, introductory statistics and group project; general empirical foundation, not successive psychology practica.
Comparative and animal neurobiology, biorhythms, models and laboratory techniques; not human neurorehabilitation.
Qualitative design/data/interpretation and group inquiry; complementary methods, not clinical interview practice.
Multivariate regression, factor analysis, AN(C)OVA, logistic and nonparametric statistics; applied data analysis, not a whole psychometrics sequence.
Memory, emotion, attention, consciousness and cognitive control with experiment evaluation/design; direct higher cognition after gateway.
Biopsychosocial health/illness, stress and medical-setting interventions; health psychology, not cognitive neuropsychology equivalent.
Neural perception and action; direct cognitive content, description-only evidence does not establish broad consciousness or rehabilitation training.
Lifespan psychopathology, diagnostic classification and biopsychosocial treatment concepts; no clinical qualification.
Physical, cognitive, emotional and social development across life; not a complete educational psychology sequence.
Systematic reviews and meta-analysis in R; existing-study synthesis, not independent primary-data psychology thesis or RP2 replacement.
Youth resilience to radicalisation and research participation; narrow applied topic, not comprehensive developmental or clinical intervention training.
Civil-society, solidarity, decolonial social theory and NGO inquiry; retained only in social route after Intro/Modern Sociology. Formal NONE does not remove preparation needs.
Rhetoric, social-psychological/neuroscientific persuasion, framing/nudging and community communication; after introductory rhetoric, not general psychological laboratory training.
Free will, time and self are conceptual complements; no general theoretical psychology equivalence.
Language production/comprehension, aphasia, development and experimental approaches; direct psycholinguistics, not rehabilitation sequence.
Psychological assessment and psychotherapy approaches across ages; conceptual clinical coursework, not supervised clinical licence training.
Philosophy of emotion, rationality, ethics and art; conceptual complement, not empirical affective-science equivalent.
Mind, consciousness, personal identity and mind-body explanations; qualified conceptual alignment.
Leadership, self-awareness, emotional intelligence and practice; organisational complement.
Leadership communication, gender/ethics/culture and emotional intelligence; not psychological diagnosis.
Modern sociological theory and imperial/colonial context; social complement and necessary preparation for advanced social theory.
Motivation, attitudes, group dynamics, culture, power/conflict and organisational change; direct organisational behaviour contribution.
Rhetoric and argumentation with writing/speaking practice; genuine preparation for advanced persuasion and Rhetoric in Action.
BATNA/ZOPA, simulations, strategic bargaining and social influence; applied workplace complement, not psychological assessment.
Primarily literary stylistics and linguistic choices, with some non-fiction application; do not relabel as organisational psychology.
Diversity, social identity, inclusive leadership and case-based practice; qualified organisational complement, description-only detail.
Public-speaking/debating education for primary-school children; requires introductory rhetoric, not educational psychology or a psychology internship.

alternatives.label: Psychology of cognition, development and behaviour
alternatives.concept: A sustained psychological and cognitive-science curriculum connects brain and behaviour, social psychology, perception, development, psychopathology and assessment. Quantitative and qualitative research and systematic review support those subjects; philosophy, sociology and rhetoric add context. Its 82.5 EC of psychology/cognitive content plus 15 EC of psychology statistics and evidence synthesis give a substantive related response, with fewer successive supervised experiments, professional-skills practica, dedicated psychometrics and no required independent psychology thesis.
alternatives.labelReason: 82.5 EC of psychology/cognition plus 15 EC psychology quantitative and evidence-synthesis courses sustain the broad label. Complementary philosophy, rhetoric and sociology are not counted as experimental psychology.
progression: Actual workbook offerings and prerequisites checked for every placement. Introductory rhetoric in Year 2 precedes advanced persuasion in Year 3. Unsupported contemporary sociology is replaced by self-contained Modern Sociology. Brain gateway and general statistics precede dependent psychology and statistical work.

alternatives.label: Social and organisational psychology
alternatives.concept: Psychology, organisational behaviour, leadership and social influence form an applied direction. Social, abnormal, developmental and assessment psychology supply 45 EC of psychological content, with 7.5 EC organisational psychology and a 30 EC general, psychological and qualitative methods/evidence-synthesis sequence. Leadership, negotiation, diversity and communication add a distinct workplace and community emphasis. This is a related interdisciplinary route, with limited dedicated experimental and professional psychology training.
alternatives.labelReason: Psychology, sociology, leadership and communication appear throughout the completed schedule, so a combined label describes it more accurately than organisational psychology alone.
progression: All actual offerings and formal prerequisites checked. General statistics precedes advanced leadership. Introductory and Modern Sociology precede advanced contemporary sociology; introductory rhetoric precedes advanced persuasion and school rhetoric practice.
alternatives.distinctness: Eight courses, 60 EC per route, differ. The primary retains neurobiology, higher cognition, perception, psycholinguistics and health psychology; the social route instead sustains organisational psychology, leadership, negotiation, diversity and communication across several years. The difference is a sustained change of disciplinary contribution, not a numerical quota. Shared clinical and developmental courses do not establish a third clinical specialisation.
traceOverrides: Examines agency, selfhood and free will as concepts behind psychological interpretations of action.

candidates.label: Developmental mental health and clinical assessment
candidates.reason: The broad route already contains the same abnormal, lifespan, health, diagnostic and youth psychology. Four alternative biomedical/public-health/ethics courses do not add a sustained distinct clinical psychology direction; withdrawn without implying clinical qualification.

candidates.label: Psychology in education and schools
candidates.reason: Education is an official application, but one lifespan course plus school public-speaking practice does not form sustained educational psychology, learning/assessment and school-intervention study. Three is a ceiling, not a reason to include an unsupported route.

candidates.label: Neurorehabilitation and recovery of cognitive function
candidates.reason: Neurobiology, perception and language provide related cognitive study but no sustained rehabilitation assessment or intervention sequence. No professional neurorehabilitation route can be manufactured from adjacent courses.

routeSelection.basis: Generic target has no domain preference. Preserve Brain & Cognition as first official-listed B3 domain, with Cognitive Neuropsychology plus Cognition, Attitude, Motivation; select permitted B2 period-2 Emotion and period-3 Development of Pro- and Antisocial Behaviour and distinct B2/B3 electives by official order. No reformed B2 domain course is imported into the older cohort. No selection based on UCR fit.

selection.assessment: Two coherent substantial responses retained. The clinical candidate duplicates the primary psychology core; its biomedical substitutions do not establish distinct clinical study. Education and rehabilitation candidates lack sustained defining content. No third alternative is justified.

notes.text: UCR sustains related psychology and cognitive science or social and organisational study, with general and psychological methods. Radboud has a denser dedicated psychology sequence, successive supervised research projects, professional-skills practica, psychometrics and a 12 EC domain thesis. UCR courses do not confer this psychology degree, clinical registration, professional qualification or automatic master admission.

audience.programmeDescription: Radboud Psychology studies human thoughts, feelings and behaviour through brain and cognition, development and mental health, and behaviour and environment. Research methods, academic and professional skills and a domain thesis are integral to the degree.
audience.comparisonExplanation: The closest UCR programme sustains psychology and cognitive science, supported by quantitative and qualitative methods, evidence synthesis and conceptual study. The second gives greater weight to organisational behaviour, leadership, diversity and communication. Both offer substantial related study while leaving gaps in dedicated psychology research projects, professional practice, psychometrics and the required independent thesis. A separate clinical programme is not shown because its psychological core repeated the closest match.

curriculum.limitation: The complete 180 EC contains 124 EC compulsory components, 40 EC restricted choices and 16 EC genuine open electives. B2 includes one theme in period 2 and one in period 3, plus one 4 EC B3 elective; that elective is not repeated in B3. B3 includes two 6 EC domain courses, three 4 EC domain electives, domain methods, ethics and a 12 EC thesis. The Development & Mental Health practical is 1 EC, explicitly confirmed by the current transition table despite an old Dutch 4 EC misprint. B1 participant hours carry 1 EC within 60; RADAr NL and B3 career orientation are mandatory without credit. B2 and B3 entry require the applicable BSA; ethics requires 90 EC psychology. The thesis requires 119 EC including Statistics 2, RP2 and full B1, with further methods knowledge assumed. Annual offerings, registration and capacities apply. This is a reconstructed completed cohort, not a promised future entrant schedule.
